beads_commands.stdout_tail: Updated tdmem-0209: Implement a dummy provider and pass mandatory conformance

argv: Accepted the deterministic standalone Rust dummy provider as executable proof that the complete M1 contract is implementable with mandatory conformance, exact idempotency, real request control, deterministic recovery, and explicit unsupported behavior.

Evidence: product/conformance/dummy-provider is an isolated Rust 2024 / Rust 1.97.1 crate with only sha2 as a direct dependency, no TraceDecay/NCM/OCEAN/path/workspace dependency, forbid(unsafe_code), deny(warnings/missing_docs), and denied unwrap/expect/panic/todo/unimplemented/dbg/stdout/stderr. It directly includes the generated provider-neutral M1 bindings and implements read-only compatible handshake/health, exact-scope idempotent observation acceptance, deterministic advisory recall with typed zero results, deterministic canonical snapshot/restore, and typed unsupported optional operations. Twenty-three named Rust journeys prove read-only identity/health, cancellation distinct from timeout, scope/generation/sequence failures, single application and duplicate acknowledgement, same-key/different-payload conflict, optional opaque extension round-trip, required extension rejection before effect, deterministic recall, deterministic snapshot bytes, restart restore, idempotent identical restore, nonempty overwrite conflict, corrupt/cross-scope snapshot rejection, and explicit unsupported feedback/maintenance. The conformance manifest partitions every accepted registry capability, the Python checker validates authority/dependency/source/test/lock/lint evidence, mutation tests reject weakened claims, and strict cargo metadata/fmt/clippy/test plus canonical contract/golden/generated-Rust drift checks pass under the pinned toolchain.
